tasks.title: Give ToolContext the open-time database size

details.goal: `ToolContext` carries the byte size of the `graph.db` the reader opened, recorded at open time, so a handler can publish a size that belongs to the generation it is answering from instead of a live `stat` of the path.
steps: Add the `dbSizeBytes` member with the doc comment above, after `config`, in the `ToolContext` interface (`:49-55`).
Rewrite the interface doc block's sentence "The five fields are the entire seam:" (`:39`) to say six fields.

Add the matching bullet at the end of that doc block, after the `config` bullet: "`dbSizeBytes` is the size recorded for the file this reader opened — read once from the file fingerprint and never re-measured, because a publish renames a new file over `graph.db` and a `stat` would describe a file this handle is not serving".

Update the module header sentence at `:4-6` (the clause at `:5` lists "the reader, the cursor pair, the logger, the clock and the resolved config") so it also names the recorded size of the file the reader opened.
Run the checks below.
details.verify: `bun run typecheck` exits 0 (proves the field is optional: no `tests/` literal was edited); `bun run lint` exits 0; `bun test tests/read-files.test.ts` is green. Done when: `grep -n "dbSizeBytes" src/shared/store/read/context.ts` shows the optional member and `grep -c "five fields" src/shared/store/read/context.ts` prints 0, and `git diff --stat` names only src/shared/store/read/context.ts.

tasks.title: Pass the open-time fingerprint size into buildContext

details.goal: `buildContext` fills `ToolContext.dbSizeBytes` from the fingerprint the store already records for the file it opened, at all three call sites, so the MCP path (`openFor`) and the CLI path (`{ ...store.context }`) both carry it.
steps: Add the third parameter `dbSizeBytes: number | null` to `buildContext` and set it on the returned object.

Add a two-line doc comment above `buildContext` saying the value is the pre-open fingerprint's `size`, so it describes the file the handle opened, and that it is the one place a payload may read a size from.
Pass `fingerprint.size` at the `openStore` call site (`:472`).
Pass `now.size` at the `refreshStore` replacement call site (`:521`).
In `openFor`, derive `dbSizeBytes` from the returned store's `fingerprint` (null when the store is not `ready`) and pass it to `buildContext` (`:978`).
Run the checks below.
details.verify: `bun run typecheck` exits 0; `bun run lint` exits 0; `bun test tests/store-refresh.test.ts tests/tools-status.test.ts` green (7 + 25 = 32 pass, unchanged — this task adds no behaviour). Done when: `grep -n "buildContext(" src/index.ts` shows the definition plus three call sites and every call passes a third argument, and `git diff --stat` names only src/index.ts.

details.goal: The two places that enumerate `ToolContext`'s members name `dbSizeBytes` and where its value comes from, so the documented seam matches the code.
details.contract:
docs/my-product/TECH-SPEC.md §6, the `ToolContext` table (`:358-366`; three columns — field | type | why it is injected rather than imported): add exactly one row after the `config` row, keeping that three-column shape:
```
| `dbSizeBytes` | `number \| null`, optional | the size recorded for the file this reader opened (the store fingerprint's `size`, taken before the handle was opened), never re-measured, so a handler cannot publish a size that belongs to a file this handle is not serving |
```
.agents/prompts/rules.md:24-25 (the `- **Tools never touch a connection.**` bullet opens at `:24`, its field list sits on `:25`): the parenthetical `(`reader`, `cursor`, `log`, `now`, `config`)` becomes `(`reader`, `cursor`, `log`, `now`, `config`, and the size recorded for the file the reader opened, `dbSizeBytes`)`. Add no sentence beyond that parenthetical; keep the surrounding two sentences and the rest of the bullet byte-identical.
Do NOT edit `docs/my-product/TOOLS-SPEC.md`; its only `size_bytes` occurrence at `:257` is an example value and no prose there defines how the number is obtained. Do not edit `docs/my-product/DATABASE.md`, `.agents/prompts/test-map.md` or `.agents/prompts/project-layout.md` (that file names `context.ts (ToolContext)` but does not enumerate members), and do not touch source or tests.
This task documents the **seam** (the field and what it means) only. The row must not claim what `status` currently publishes: phase 0 changes no handler, so no sentence here may state that `status.graph.size_bytes` already reports the opened size. Nothing in phase 0 asserts that derivation and no document specifies it.
steps: Add the `dbSizeBytes` row, with the type cell `number | null`, optional, to the `ToolContext` table in docs/my-product/TECH-SPEC.md (`:358-366`) after the `config` row.
Replace the five-name parenthetical on .agents/prompts/rules.md:25 with the six-name form above; leave the bullet's prose and `:24` opening untouched.
Check both files with the greps below.
Run the checks below.
details.verify: `git diff --stat` names only docs/my-product/TECH-SPEC.md and .agents/prompts/rules.md. Done when: `grep -n 'dbSizeBytes' docs/my-product/TECH-SPEC.md .agents/prompts/rules.md` returns exactly one hit in each file, `grep -c 'now`, `config`)' .agents/prompts/rules.md` prints 0 (the old five-name list is gone; the pattern is single-quoted so the backticks stay literal), the added table row has three cells, and `bun test tests/instructions.test.ts` is green (that test pins `INSTRUCTIONS_TEXT`, which neither edited file feeds).

tasks.title: Phase 0 gate: seam and plumbing verify

details.goal: Prove the seam exists, the plumbing fills it, and nothing else moved, before phase 1 builds behaviour on it.
details.contract: Read-only gate: this task owns no files and must not edit any. `{ ...store.context }` call sites and `tests/` fakes are untouched by design, so any test edit here is a defect to report, not to make.
steps: Run `bun run typecheck` from the repository root and record the exit code.
Run `bun run lint` and record the exit code.
Run `bun test tests/read-files.test.ts tests/store-refresh.test.ts tests/tools-status.test.ts` and record pass/fail counts.

Run `git status --porcelain -z | tr '\0' '\n'` (or plain `git status --porcelain`) and confirm the only modifications are the plan's own files. Porcelain collapses untracked directories to one entry, so the expected output is exactly four unstaged-modification lines of the form ` M <path>` (porcelain's first column is the index, so a working-tree edit starts with a space): ` M src/shared/store/read/context.ts`, ` M src/index.ts`, ` M docs/my-product/TECH-SPEC.md`, ` M .agents/prompts/rules.md`, plus the two untracked plan directories `?? .ppm/fix-ghissue13/` and `?? .ppm/fix-ghissue14/`. `.ppm/fix-ghissue14/` belongs to another planner, predates this plan's work and is out of scope; any other path, or a change inside `.ppm/fix-ghissue14/`, is reported and never repaired.
Run `stat -c '%s %Y' .sangkar/graph.db` and confirm it still prints `4677632 1795158731`; report any other reading as a blocking defect instead of touching the file.
details.verify: Done when `bun run typecheck` exits 0, `bun run lint` exits 0, `bun test tests/read-files.test.ts tests/store-refresh.test.ts tests/tools-status.test.ts` reports `54 pass / 0 fail` (22 + 7 + 25, the measured baseline — no test file is edited in this phase), `git status --porcelain` lists exactly the four modified plan files of this phase plus the two untracked plan directories `?? .ppm/fix-ghissue13/` and `?? .ppm/fix-ghissue14/` and nothing else (`.ppm/fix-ghissue14/` is pre-existing and out of scope; a mismatch is reported, never repaired), and `stat -c '%s %Y' .sangkar/graph.db` still prints `4677632 1795158731`. Record every command's output tail in `progress`.
